coachingPoints: Aim the bounce about two-thirds of the way to your target — the ball should arrive at waist height.
Push through the pass, not down at the floor; the bounce is a byproduct, not the goal.
Step into it like a chest pass — same footwork, different target zone.
The lower the bounce point, the slower the pass — against close defenders, bounce it closer to yourself.
Keep it crisp; a slow bounce pass is just a turnover waiting to happen.
commonMistakes: Aiming the bounce too close to your own feet — the ball arrives at the receiver's shins.
Throwing it too hard at the floor — it rockets past the target's hands.
Using it when a direct chest pass is open — bounce passes are slower; don't use them unnecessarily.
One-handing it lazily across your body — weak angle, easy steal.
description: The pass that goes under the defense — bounce it around outstretched arms and into a teammate's hands.
gameSituations: Feeding the post against a fronting defender — bounce it to the low side.
Against a zone defense with high hands — bounce it through the gaps.
Entry passes when the defender overplays the passing lane.

howTo.detail: Hold the ball at chest or waist height, same grip as a chest pass. Decide your target — usually a post player or a cutter — and picture the bounce point.
howTo.title: Read the defender's hands

howTo.detail: Step toward the target. Your step sells direction and adds power, exactly like a chest pass.
howTo.title: Step into the pass

howTo.detail: Aim your release at a spot on the floor roughly two-thirds of the distance to your teammate. Push the ball forward and slightly down — think 'through the floor,' not 'at the floor.'
howTo.title: Target the two-thirds bounce point

howTo.detail: Snap your wrists and follow through toward the target. The ball should hit the floor once and arrive at the receiver's waist — never at their feet.
howTo.title: Snap and follow through

title: Bounce Pass
whatIsIt: The bounce pass is a two-handed pass that hits the floor once between you and your teammate. It travels under the defender's hands instead of through them, making it the safest pass in traffic.

Where a chest pass flies straight into outstretched arms, the bounce pass ducks underneath. It's the classic post-entry pass and the go-to option when a defender is playing the passing lane aggressively.
whyItMatters: Defenders are taught to get their hands up and deflect passes. The bounce pass punishes that: hands up means hands can't reach the floor. Learning when to bounce and when to go direct is a core part of basketball IQ — the right pass type turns turnovers into easy baskets.
